text:
sara.arch: Quick follow-up from the CP split RFC — can we run a short experiment with a per-tenant controlplane-lite gateway? trying to validate handshake surface and failure modes before we commit to the full refactor.

mike-net: +1. main concerns: cert propagation, DNS mapping, and how we fail over to regional shared CP when tenant gateways are overloaded.

julie-plat: Agree. Also need to lock down the API contract for the gateway -> controlplane handshake. We should avoid adding new long-lived secrets in the controlplane.

kevin-sre: two operational points: 1) how do we rotate CA for tenant gateways without forcing mass reconnects, 2) visibility for oncall (which metrics?)

sara.arch: For the handshake surface I'm proposing a lightweight tokenized bootstrap + short-lived mTLS cert issued after handshake. sketch:
```
cp_gateway:
  mode: lite
  handshake: token
  bootstrap_ttl: 5m
  cert_issuer: redwood-ephemeral-ca
  cert_ttl: 1h
```
This keeps initial auth simple and keeps traffic mTLS afterwards. Thoughts?

mike-net: token bootstrap is fine. but how do we store/rotate the token? we can't force customers to have long lived tokens. Suggest using per-deployment short-lived token minted by controlplane when customer onboards the gateway. store it in customer vault, rotate via rollout.

julie-plat: If we use ephemeral certs we need a cheap OCSP/CRL check. Or just accept short TTLs and rely on reenrollment. For on-prem we should support an offline-enrollment flow.

kevin-sre: For CA rotation: timeline idea — dual-sign: new CA signs new certs while old CA still trusted for verification. drains: gracefully rotate gateway pools. Metrics: handshake_success_rate, handshake_latency_p95, gateway_failover_count, enroll_rate, cert_renew_failures. Add synth check to verify chain on every restart.

sara.arch: Good. Failure/fallback behaviour: if tenant gateway is unreachable or overloaded we want a deterministic fallback to the regional shared-controlplane. Proposal: gateway advertises an affinity token and health score. Router policy: prefer tenant gateway if health_score > 0.8 else route to shared CP. Syncs every 30s.

mike-net: That policy sounds reasonable. Need to simulate link flaps; can we run chaos tests that kill gateway nodes and ensure the route switch doesn't create session storms?

julie-plat: Also think about DNS: customer-private endpoints will need per-tenant DNS delegations or an SRV pattern. I prefer delegations (cleaner cert boundaries) but it's operationally heavier.

sara.arch: Agree on delegation. Plan: provide two onboarding options — delegated DNS (preferred) and proxy-path (temporary). Documented in the onboarding playbook.

kevin-sre: Ops checklist for the experiment:
- run 2 tenants in GA regions (low traffic)
- instrument metrics listed above
- run fault-injection for 5m windows
- validate CA rotation path with dual-signing
- verify fallback to shared CP under overload load test

julie-plat: Can we extend rollout control so tenants can opt into 'gateway-lite' via a feature flag? that makes rollback trivial.

sara.arch: yes — feature-flag + canary percentage. rollout plan: 0 -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% (per-tenant groups), hold 24h at each stage.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: experiment feature-flag scaffold created in canary service. CI green.

mike-net: I'll add a small spike to the simulator to model DNS delegation failover and session churn. ETA EOD Thursday.

kevin-sre: I'll own the runbook for CA rotation and the oncall playbook for gateway flaps.

sara.arch: action items:
- mike-net: simulator spike + chaos tests (EOD Thu)
- kevin-sre: runbook + metrics dash (Mon)
- julie-plat: onboarding docs (delegation + proxy path) (Mon)
- sara.arch: coordinate two tenant pilots and feature-flag rollout plan (this week)

sara.arch: thanks all, we'll sync Friday after initial tests. :thumbsup:
